Post-VPN-auth Qilin ransomware staging behavior on internal hosts AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-compromise activity Qilin operators perform after pivoting through a Check Point VPN tunnel: shadow-copy deletion, BCDedit recovery disablement, Defender tampering, and ESXi vmkfstools/vim-cmd invocation within minutes of a new VPN-pool logon. Stitches CommonSecurityLog VPN auth to endpoint behavior. Rationale: Stitches the article's exploit vector (Check Point VPN auth) to the named threat (Qilin RaaS) by joining VPN-assigned client logons to recovery-inhibition behavior within 2h — a tight time-window correlation that drops the FP rate well below a standalone vssadmin-delete query. Cross-checked Qilin TTPs against MITRE ATT&CK G1032 and prior public Qilin IR write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1032/ • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1490 T1562.001 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Veeam, Commvault, or Acronis pre-snapshot shadow-copy cleanup
  • Sysadmin troubleshooting Windows Update via DISM/wbadmin
  • GPO-driven Defender policy changes during scheduled maintenance window
  • Pen-test red team running PowerSploit modules during an authorized engagement
  • SCCM/MECM deploying a Defender configuration baseline that toggles DisableRealtimeMonitoring temporarily
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("veeamsvc","backupadmin","sccm-svc") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("VeeamBackupSvc.exe","BeMonitor.exe","CcmExec.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the AuthTime + MinutesAfterAuth fields — if the VPN logon came from a Check Point gateway and the recovery-inhibition fired within 30 min, treat as confirmed pending IP check. Pull the source IP from CommonSecurityLog and confirm whether it matches the 8 Qilin indicators. 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, force-revoke the VPN session, disable the user account, kick all sessions on the gateway pool, and apply the Check Point IKEv2-only mitigation if not already deployed. 3) Hunt: scan all hosts reached from the VPN pool in the last 30d for the Qilin payload MD5s, .qilin extensions, esxcli/vim-cmd VM-kill commands, and lateral PsExec/WMI from the entry host.
let WindowMin = 120m;
let VpnAuthHosts = DeviceLogonEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
    | where LogonType == "Network" or LogonType == "RemoteInteractive"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Private"  // VPN-pool client IPs are RFC1918
    | project AuthTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteIP;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shadow","delete"))
     or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "shadowcopy" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete")
     or (FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine has "bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures" or ProcessCommandLine has "recoveryenabled" and ProcessCommandLine has "No"))
     or (FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("catalog","systemstatebackup"))
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring","Set-MpPreference -DisableBehaviorMonitoring","Remove-MpPreference"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner VpnAuthHosts on DeviceName
| where Timestamp between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + WindowMin)
| project Timestamp, AuthTime, MinutesAfterAuth=datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, AuthTime), DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 120m;
let VpnAuthHosts = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
    | where EventID == 4624
    | where LogonType in (3, 10)
    | where IpAddress startswith "10." or IpAddress startswith "192.168." or IpAddress matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\."
    | project AuthTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, IpAddress;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith "\\vssadmin.exe" and CommandLine has_all ("shadow","delete"))
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "shadowcopy" and CommandLine has "delete")
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\bcdedit.exe" and (CommandLine has "bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures" or CommandLine has "recoveryenabled" and CommandLine has "No"))
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wbadmin.exe" and CommandLine has "delete" and CommandLine has_any ("catalog","systemstatebackup"))
     or (NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has_any ("Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring","Set-MpPreference -DisableBehaviorMonitoring"))
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner VpnAuthHosts on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + WindowMin)
| project TimeGenerated, AuthTime, MinutesAfterAuth=datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, AuthTime), Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, IpAddress
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:(4688 OR 1)) (@CommandLine:(*"shadowcopy delete"* OR *"shadows /all"* OR *"bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures"* OR *"recoveryenabled No"* OR *"DisableRealtimeMonitoring"* OR *"delete catalog"*)) (@Image:(*\vssadmin.exe OR *\VSSAdmin.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\WMIC.exe OR *\bcdedit.exe OR *\BCDEdit.exe OR *\wbadmin.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ((ImageFileName=/\\vssadmin\.exe$/i CommandLine=/shadow.*delete/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\wmic\.exe$/i CommandLine=/shadowcopy.*delete/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\bcdedit\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(bootstatuspolicy\s+ignoreallfailures|recoveryenabled\s+No)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\wbadmin\.exe$/i CommandLine=/delete.*(catalog|systemstatebackup)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/Set-MpPreference.*Disable(Realtime|Behavior)Monitoring/i)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("vssadmin.exe","wmic.exe","bcdedit.exe","wbadmin.exe","powershell.exe") AND Processes.process IN ("*shadowcopy delete*","*shadows /all*","*delete catalog*","*bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures*","*recoveryenabled No*","*Set-MpPreference*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*")) by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("vssadmin.exe","wmic.exe","bcdedit.exe","wbadmin.exe","powershell.exe") AND Processes.process IN ("*shadowcopy delete*","*shadows /all*","*delete catalog*","*bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures*","*recoveryenabled No*","*Set-MpPreference*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*")) by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("45.77.149.152", "209.182.225.136", "38.60.157.139", "162.33.177.101", "45.76.26.42", "144.208.127.155", "38.54.88.201", "38.54.107.167", "66.42.99.200") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["45.77.149.152", "209.182.225.136", "38.60.157.139", "162.33.177.101", "45.76.26.42", "144.208.127.155", "38.54.88.201", "38.54.107.167", "66.42.99.200"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Google patches new Chrome zero-day flaw exploited in the wild

BleepingComputer
2026-06-09 5 use cases 0 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Google has released emergency updates to patch another Chrome zero-day vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild, the fifth such flaw patched since the start of the year. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Endpoints running Chrome below patched build for CVE-2026-11645
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Chrome navigation to low-reputation domain immediately preceding renderer crash
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Cluster of Chrome renderer crashes via WerFault across multiple hosts
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] chrome.exe spawning LOLBin child process (post-V8 sandbox escape)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Endpoints running Chrome below patched build for CVE-2026-11645 AIWeaponization High
Inventory hunt that surfaces hosts still on Chrome versions older than 149.0.7827.102 (Windows/Linux) or 149.0.7827.103 (macOS), or with CVE-2026-11645 / -2441 / -3909 / -3910 / -5281 reported by the TVM/vuln scanner. These endpoints are exposed to the in-the-wild V8 OOB R/W zero-day until they roll forward. Rationale: Anchors on the exact CVE IDs (CVE-2026-11645 plus the four prior 2026 Chrome zero-days) and the fixed build numbers 149.0.7827.102/103 named in the article — deterministic, low-FP exposure hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/
ATT&CKT1189 T1203
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Chrome auto-update pending reboot — version flips after restart
  • Hosts in 'managed' channel deliberately pinned to an older milestone (e.g. legacy app compatibility)
  • Linux endpoints using distro-packaged Chromium (different version string format)
  • Kiosk/IoT devices intentionally air-gapped and not patched
  • TVM scanner cache lag where the host actually updated within the last hour
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "149.0.7827." and SoftwareVersion !startswith "149.0.7828."
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm the reported SoftwareVersion against the host's live `chrome://version` or the registry build value; rule out scanner staleness. Cross-check device against Defender for any renderer crash or anomalous chrome.exe child in the last 7 days (UC2/UC3). Step 2 — Contain: Push the Chrome MSI/PKG update via SCCM/Intune/JAMF and force-relaunch; if not possible immediately, block egress for chrome.exe via host firewall policy until patched. Step 3 — Hunt: Pull DeviceNetworkEvents for the same DeviceId scoped to chrome.exe and check for visits to newly-registered or low-reputation domains in the 24h window before the inventory snapshot, plus pivot to UC4 to spot probable exploitation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-11645","CVE-2026-2441","CVE-2026-3909","CVE-2026-3910","CVE-2026-5281")
| where SoftwareName has "chrome" and SoftwareVendor =~ "google"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, SoftwareVersion) by DeviceId, SoftwareName) on DeviceId, SoftwareName
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-11645","CVE-2026-2441","CVE-2026-3909","CVE-2026-3910","CVE-2026-5281")
| where SoftwareName has "chrome" and SoftwareVendor =~ "google"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-11645","CVE-2026-2441","CVE-2026-3909","CVE-2026-3910","CVE-2026-5281") AND Vulnerabilities.signature="*Chrome*" by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.cve, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.signature

Cluster of Chrome renderer crashes via WerFault across multiple hosts AIExploitation Medium
Alerts when WerFault.exe is spawned by chrome.exe at burst rates or across multiple distinct hosts within a short window — the heap-corruption signature of CVE-2026-11645 attempted exploitation (the article explicitly notes the bug can trigger a crash). Single user crashes are noise; clustered crashes against the same site visit pattern are exploitation telemetry. Rationale: Article explicitly states the V8 OOB R/W bug can 'trigger a crash' alongside info disclosure / RCE — burst crashes are the operationally observable phase. Pivot is WerFault parented by chrome.exe (article-specific to the Chrome process model), with threshold to suppress single-user noise. Cross-checked against: • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/
ATT&CKT1499.004 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bad Chrome extension causing widespread crashes (e.g. broken update of a popular ad-blocker)
  • GPU driver regression after a Windows Update KB
  • Corporate VPN client interfering with QUIC/HTTP3 and crashing renderer
  • Chrome instability after a forced policy push (e.g. site-isolation toggle)
  • Hardware fault on a shared image (bad RAM module on a fleet of identical VDIs)
Suppression filter
| where SampleCmd !has "--type=crashpad-handler"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull the hosts in the burst and check the site visit history (UC4 join) for a common domain in the 60s preceding each crash. Confirm Chrome version against UC1 — if hosts are already on 149.0.7827.102+, suspect non-exploit cause. Step 2 — Contain: If hosts are unpatched and a common URL appears, sinkhole the domain at proxy/DNS, block at perimeter firewall, and force-push the Chrome update to the affected fleet via Intune/SCCM. Isolate any host with a post-crash anomaly (UC3 child process) via Defender Live Response. Step 3 — Hunt: Sweep DeviceNetworkEvents for any other endpoints that contacted the suspect URL in the last 14 days; pull HAR via proxy logs for the page payload and submit to a sandbox for V8 exploit indicators (heap-spray patterns, WebAssembly abuse).
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where FileName =~ "WerFault.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| summarize CrashCount = count(), DistinctHosts = dcount(DeviceId), SampleDevices = make_set(DeviceName, 10), FirstCrash = min(Timestamp), LastCrash = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine) by bin(Timestamp, WindowMinutes)
| where DistinctHosts >= 3 or CrashCount >= 10
| project FirstCrash, LastCrash, CrashCount, DistinctHosts, SampleDevices, SampleCmd
| order by FirstCrash desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventLog == "Application" and EventID == 1000
| where RenderedDescription has_any ("chrome.exe", "chrome_child.dll") or ParameterXml has_any ("chrome.exe", "chrome_child.dll")
| summarize CrashCount = count(), DistinctHosts = dcount(Computer), SampleHosts = make_set(Computer, 10), FirstCrash = min(TimeGenerated), LastCrash = max(TimeGenerated) by bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where DistinctHosts >= 3 or CrashCount >= 10
| order by FirstCrash desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\CHROME.EXE) @Image:(*\\WerFault.exe OR *\\werfault.exe OR *\\WERFAULT.EXE)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/werfault\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/chrome\.exe$/i
| groupBy([bucket(_time, 30m, as=bucket), aid, ComputerName], function=count(as=CrashCount))
| groupBy([bucket], function={count(as=CrashCount) | count(field=aid, distinct=true, as=DistinctHosts)})
| DistinctHosts>=3 OR CrashCount>=10

| tstats summariesonly=true count, dc(Processes.dest) as DistinctHosts, values(Processes.dest) as hosts from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="WerFault.exe" AND Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" by _time, span=30m
| `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")`
| where DistinctHosts >= 3 OR count >= 10
| sort - _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Processes.dest) as DistinctHosts, values(Processes.dest) as hosts from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="WerFault.exe" AND Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" by _time, span=30m
| `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")`
| where DistinctHosts >= 3 OR count >= 10

chrome.exe spawning LOLBin child process (post-V8 sandbox escape) AIInstallation High
Hunts for chrome.exe directly parenting cmd/powershell/mshta/regsvr32/rundll32/wscript/cscript/bitsadmin/certutil — the article's described arbitrary-code-execution-in-renderer outcome of CVE-2026-11645 manifests, after sandbox escape, as one of these LOLBin children. Chrome legitimately spawns only a small whitelist of children (chrome_crashpad_handler, software_reporter_tool, GoogleUpdate); anything else is high-fidelity. Rationale: Chrome's process tree is well-known and tightly bounded — any LOLBin child is high-signal regardless of cmdline. The article's specific claim of 'arbitrary code execution inside the web browser's sandbox' becomes operationally visible only when the renderer escapes and spawns one of these binaries. Cross-checked against: • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
ATT&CKT1203 T1059.001 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Chrome Enterprise policy-deployed extensions invoking certutil for cert-pinning operations
  • Webex/Zoom click-to-call handlers spawning cmd.exe via custom URL scheme
  • Power BI / Tableau native messaging hosts spawning powershell.exe
  • User-installed dev extensions (e.g. Postman) firing curl.exe
  • Corporate SSO helper invoking rundll32 against a credprovider DLL
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildImage endswith @"\rundll32.exe" and ChildCmd has_any ("davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie", "shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL")) and not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--type=utility")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Capture the full ChildCmd and decode any -EncodedCommand / base64; correlate with the parent chrome.exe network connections in the 5 min before the spawn to find the lure URL. Pull the renderer SHA256 and check it against Chrome's signed-binary baseline. Step 2 — Contain: Isolate the host via Defender Live Response / CS RTR, kill the chrome.exe tree, collect a memory image for V8 exploit reversing, and revoke any AAD refresh tokens the user holds. Step 3 — Hunt: Sweep DeviceNetworkEvents for the lure URL across the org and check UrlClickEvents / EmailUrlInfo to find the delivery vector; pivot to UC4 to confirm the time-correlation pattern, and add the SHA256 of any dropped payload to ThreatIntelligenceIndicator.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe","wmic.exe","forfiles.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage = FolderPath, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\chrome.exe" or ParentProcessName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe","wmic.exe","forfiles.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Chrome.exe Spawning Unexpected LOLBin Child Process (CVE-2026-11645 Post-Exploitation)
id: 6b8a7d34-1c1f-4f9a-9c80-9a92cbbac4a9
description: Detects chrome.exe directly parenting cmd/powershell/mshta/regsvr32/rundll32/wscript/cscript/bitsadmin/certutil — a strong V8-sandbox-escape signal during CVE-2026-11645 in-the-wild exploitation.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-patches-fifth-chrome-zero-day-bug-exploited-in-attacks-this-year/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1218
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\chrome.exe'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msbuild.exe'
      - '\installutil.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
      - '\forfiles.exe'
  condition: parent and child
fields:
  - ParentImage
  - ParentCommandLine
  - Image
  - CommandLine
  - User
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\CHROME.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\msbuild.exe OR *\\installutil.exe OR *\\wmic.exe OR *\\forfiles.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/chrome\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget|msbuild|installutil|wmic|forfiles)\.exe$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| table([_time, aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count, values(Processes.process) as cmd, values(Processes.process_hash) as hash, min(_time) as firstSeen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe","wmic.exe","forfiles.exe") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")`
| sort - firstSeen
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Processes.process) as cmd, values(Processes.process_hash) as hash, min(_time) as firstSeen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msbuild.exe","installutil.exe","wmic.exe","forfiles.exe") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")`
| sort - firstSeen
Chrome navigation to low-reputation domain immediately preceding renderer crash AIDelivery Medium
Time-window join surfacing the article's drive-by exploitation pattern: chrome.exe contacts an external URL (the 'crafted HTML page' delivery vector for CVE-2026-11645) and a renderer crash (WerFault parented by chrome.exe / Application Error 1000) follows on the same host within ~120 seconds. The pairing is the classic shape of a heap-corruption browser exploit attempt. Rationale: Article calls out the delivery primitive ('crafted HTML pages') and the impact primitive ('triggering a crash') as both being outputs of CVE-2026-11645; the high-fidelity signal is the temporal pairing of an external Chrome HTTP request and a renderer crash. ImWebSession + Event(EID 1000) is the cleanest Sentinel path that doesn't depend on Defender XDR ingestion. Cross-checked against: • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1189/
ATT&CKT1189 T1203 T1499.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Page with a broken WebGL/WebGPU asset crashing renderer after legit nav (common on internal dashboards using outdated three.js builds)
  • Bad ad creative crashing renderer on a popular news site
  • Streaming video with a faulty codec triggering renderer death
  • User power-cycling the host during a normal browsing session (WerFault collateral)
  • Site visited via prefetch/preload then user closes tab — crash unrelated
Suppression filter
| where RemoteUrl !endswith "google.com" and RemoteUrl !endswith "gstatic.com" and RemoteUrl !endswith "googleapis.com" and RemoteUrl !endswith "googleusercontent.com"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Reputation-check the RemoteUrl/Url against VirusTotal + URLscan + DomainTools (look for newly-registered TLDs, suspicious WHOIS, no Alexa/Tranco rank). Pull the HAR via proxy and inspect for inline <script> with large typed-array allocations or WebAssembly modules — the V8 OOB primitive setup. Step 2 — Contain: Blackhole the domain at proxy/secure web gateway, block IP at perimeter, force-isolate the affected host. Push UC1 patch verification across the org for any host that also visited the URL. Step 3 — Hunt: Sweep all DeviceNetworkEvents for the same domain/IP for 30 days back. Cross-check whether the user was hit via an in-org link (email phishing, Teams/Slack message) — pull UrlClickEvents and EmailUrlInfo. Look for UC3 hits on the same hosts to confirm sandbox escape.
let WindowSeconds = 120;
let Crashes = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(24h)
    | where FileName =~ "WerFault.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
    | project CrashTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| join kind=inner Crashes on DeviceId
| where CrashTime between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project Timestamp, CrashTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', CrashTime, Timestamp), DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowSeconds = 120;
let Crashes = Event
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where EventLog == "Application" and EventID == 1000
    | where RenderedDescription has "chrome.exe" or ParameterXml has "chrome.exe"
    | project CrashTime = TimeGenerated, Computer;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Chrome", "Chromium")
| where isnotempty(Url)
| join kind=inner Crashes on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where CrashTime between (TimeGenerated .. TimeGenerated + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project TimeGenerated, CrashTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', CrashTime, TimeGenerated), DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/werfault\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/chrome\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/chrome\.exe$/i (RemotePort=443 OR RemotePort=80)}, field=[aid], include=[RemoteAddressIP4, _time], key=ConnTime)
| DelaySec := _time - ConnTime
| DelaySec>=0 AND DelaySec<=120
| table([_time, ConnTime, DelaySec, aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4])
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="WerFault.exe" AND Processes.parent_process_name="chrome.exe" by _time, Processes.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name("Processes")`

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-42271 (CVSS score: 8.7), is a command injection vulnerability that could allow any authenticated user to run arbitrary commands on the

LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 MCP test endpoint POST (preview command injection) AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP POSTs to LiteLLM's vulnerable MCP test endpoints (/mcp-rest/test/connection and /mcp-rest/test/tools/list) that accept full stdio server configurations and spawn arbitrary commands as the proxy user. Both endpoints are pre-patch attacker entrypoints called out by BerriAI and Horizon3.ai. Rationale: Both URIs are named verbatim in BerriAI's advisory and the article as the only two endpoints that accepted stdio command/args/env in the request body pre-1.83.7. Any POST to these paths is a high-fidelity exploit signal. Cross-checked Horizon3.ai write-up and BerriAI security advisory. Defender Advanced Hunting has no clean inbound-HTTP request table, so defender_kql left empty; primary surface is reverse-proxy / IIS / WAF logs (sentinel_kql + datadog_query). Cross-checked against: • https://www.horizon3.ai/ • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised pen-test or vulnerability scanner (Tenable, Qualys, Nuclei) probing for CVE-2026-42271
  • Internal admin testing MCP server configuration via the preview workflow before save (legitimate pre-1.83.7 usage)
  • Post-patch admin role traffic to the same URI (now PROXY_ADMIN-gated — verify role binding)
  • Synthetic monitoring (Datadog Synthetics, Pingdom) hitting LiteLLM endpoints that happen to share the path prefix
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("<known scanner CIDRs>", "<internal admin CIDRs>")
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","Nuclei","qualys","tenable","DatadogSynthetics")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull source IP, auth header / csUserName, and request body if logged; check the body for `command`, `args`, `env` JSON keys, and confirm LiteLLM version < 1.83.7 on the target. 2) Contain: block both URIs at the reverse proxy / WAF, rotate the proxy master key and every model-provider API key stored by LiteLLM, restart the LiteLLM container to kill any spawned subprocesses. 3) Hunt: on the LiteLLM host pivot to DeviceProcessEvents where InitiatingProcessFileName has python/uvicorn within ±5 minutes of each POST (UC2 logic), pull all outbound from the host since the first POST, check for new ASEP / cron entries and reads of /root/.aws, .env or kubeconfig.

| order by TimeGenerated desc

LiteLLM proxy (uvicorn/python) spawning shell or LOLBin — CVE-2026-42271 post-exploit AIInstallation High
Detects child processes spawned by the LiteLLM proxy process (python/uvicorn running litellm) where the child is a shell, network downloader, or recon binary inconsistent with normal LiteLLM operation. CVE-2026-42271 spawns the attacker-supplied command as a subprocess of the proxy process — this is the host-side fingerprint of successful exploitation. Rationale: BerriAI's advisory and the article both state the proxy 'spawned the supplied command as a subprocess on the proxy host with the privileges of the proxy process'. The parent process is therefore python/uvicorn running litellm.proxy. Any shell / curl / whoami child of that exact parent is the canonical post-exploit fingerprint and rare in normal LiteLLM operation. Cross-checked BerriAI advisory and Horizon3.ai analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://www.horizon3.ai/ • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • LiteLLM custom callback / plugin shelling out to `curl` for webhook delivery or to `aws`/`gcloud` for cloud-key resolution
  • DB migration script running `alembic upgrade` or `prisma migrate` at container start (parent uvicorn -> bash -> migrate)
  • Health-check / readiness probe running `whoami` or `id` for diagnostics
  • Pen-test or red-team intentionally exercising CVE-2026-42271 against a staging deployment
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("alembic upgrade","prisma migrate","pip install","--health","healthcheck")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("--health","migrate")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull full ProcessCommandLine of the child, InitiatingProcessId, and the connecting RemoteIP from DeviceNetworkEvents within ±60s. Confirm LiteLLM version < 1.83.7 on the host. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender / Falcon network containment, stop the LiteLLM container, rotate every secret stored by the proxy (model provider API keys, DB creds, SSO secrets) and any cloud IAM role attached to the host. 3) Hunt: enumerate all child processes of the same LiteLLM PID for the last 7d, all outbound DNS / network connects from the proxy process, new ASEP / cron / systemd unit writes, and reads of /root/.aws, /root/.kube, .env or model-key files. Pivot to other LiteLLM hosts in the fleet for the same parent->child shape.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","python3.exe","uvicorn","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("litellm","litellm.proxy","litellm.main","--port 4000")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","nslookup","dig","whoami","id","uname","chmod","base64")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessId, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("litellm","litellm.proxy","--port 4000")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","nslookup","dig","whoami","id","uname","chmod","base64")

Anomalous Host header to LiteLLM (Starlette CVE-2026-48710 BadHost bypass) AIExploitation Medium
Detects HTTP requests to LiteLLM that carry a Host header outside the deployment's baseline of expected hosts, especially when reaching auth-gated paths. CVE-2026-48710 abuses Starlette's host header validation so an attacker can submit a forged Host to bypass LiteLLM's auth and reach the vulnerable MCP test endpoints unauthenticated. Rationale: Horizon3.ai chained CVE-2026-48710 (Starlette BadHost) with CVE-2026-42271 to reach LiteLLM's MCP test endpoints unauthenticated, and the article's mitigation guidance explicitly calls out reviewing logs for 'unusual Host header activity'. The on-wire signature is a request whose Host header is forged or unexpected for the deployment. Defender / Falcon FDR don't ship HTTP request data so those fields are empty; primary surface is HTTP access logs. Cross-checked Horizon3.ai analysis and Starlette security advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.horizon3.ai/ • https://github.com/encode/starlette/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal scanner or load balancer health probe sending an IP-literal Host header instead of the DNS name
  • New legitimate LiteLLM hostname added to the deployment that isn't yet in the 30d baseline
  • Kubernetes ingress / service mesh sidecar (Istio, Linkerd) rewriting Host on internal traffic
  • Developer hitting LiteLLM via `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` while debugging in a non-prod environment
Suppression filter
| where CsHost !in ("localhost","127.0.0.1","<known internal probe hosts>")
| where CIp !startswith "10."  // tune to your private ranges
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the Host value, source IP and full URI; confirm Starlette version ≤ 1.0.0 in the LiteLLM deployment's dependency tree (`pip show starlette`); check whether the source IP is inside the corporate perimeter or external. 2) Contain: front LiteLLM with a strict Host allowlist at the reverse proxy / WAF and drop unknown Host values; upgrade Starlette to ≥ 1.0.1 and LiteLLM to ≥ 1.83.7; rotate model provider keys and proxy admin tokens. 3) Hunt: pivot to the LiteLLM host's DeviceProcessEvents / ProcessRollup2 for python/uvicorn parents spawning shells in the same window (UC2), and pull all outbound network from the LiteLLM host since the first anomalous Host header to look for credential exfil.
// Targets Azure App Service deployments of LiteLLM (AppServiceHTTPLogs carries CsHost).
// For IIS-fronted / WAF-fronted deployments, pull Host from the upstream WAF custom field.
let Baseline = AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1h))
    | summarize by _ResourceId, CsHost;
AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where CsMethod =~ "POST"
| where CsUriStem startswith "/mcp-rest/" or CsUriStem in~ ("/chat/completions","/v1/chat/completions","/key/generate")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on _ResourceId, CsHost
| project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, CsHost, CsMethod, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, CIp, UserAgent, ScStatus
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-11645 — Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Read and Write Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-09 1 use case 0 techniques 2 kill-chain phases detected

Google Chromium V8 out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page. This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera. Vendor: Google, Product: Chromium V8. Federal patch due: 2026-06-23.

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
